checks.name: plausibility::facility_size
checks.description: Median facility size. A CLO holds a few hundred positions in loans that are themselves much larger — the deal takes a slice. Positions of a few hundred thousand to a few million are the usual range.

checks.name: plausibility::spread
checks.description: Median margin over the reference rate, in basis points. European term loan B pricing has sat in the high 300s to low 500s for years.

checks.name: plausibility::market_price
checks.description: Median secondary price per 100 of par. Performing European loans trade near par; a median below the high 80s would mean a distressed book.

checks.name: plausibility::maturity
checks.description: Median original term. Leveraged loans are written for five to eight years, and a CLO's reinvestment rules assume that horizon.

checks.name: plausibility::leverage
checks.description: Median net debt to EBITDA. Below about 3.5x a borrower is not leveraged; much above 7x the loan is not broadly syndicated.

checks.name: plausibility::rating_mix
checks.description: Share of the opening book in the single-B bucket. Leveraged loans are overwhelmingly single-B; a book that were not would be a different asset class.

checks.name: plausibility::ccc_at_close
checks.description: CCC and below at close. Indentures cap this around 7.5%, and a deal prices with headroom beneath the cap rather than against it. Measured at the opening cut-off: migration is expected to push it up later, and that rise is the thing the CCC chart exists to show.

checks.name: plausibility::country_spread
checks.description: Distinct obligor countries. A European CLO spans several jurisdictions by construction; one or two would not be a European deal.

checks.name: plausibility::industry_spread
checks.description: Distinct industries. Diversity requirements make a concentrated book impossible to place.

checks.name: plausibility::seniority
checks.description: Senior secured share. Indentures generally require at least 90% senior secured, so a book much below that could not be issued.

checks.name: plausibility::covenant_lite
checks.description: Covenant-lite share. European issuance has been overwhelmingly covenant-lite since around 2018.

checks.name: non_negative_columns
checks.description: These never go below zero: current_balance, current_par, market_value, recovery_amount, realised_loss, months_to_maturity.

checks.name: custom::credit_factor_matches_the_rating
checks.description: Every facility's credit factor is the one its grade maps to. The factor is what the average credit quality is computed from, so a factor that has drifted from the rating would corrupt the headline figure while every rating on the tape still looked right.

checks.name: custom::credit_factor_is_monotone_in_the_grade
checks.description: A worse grade never carries a lower factor. This is what makes the weighted average mean anything: if the ordering broke, a downgrade could improve the reported credit quality.

checks.name: custom::no_duplicate_facility_cutoff
checks.description: One row per facility per cut-off.

checks.name: custom::market_value_ties_to_par_and_price
checks.description: Market value is par times price over 100, to the cent.

checks.name: custom::maturity_after_origination
checks.description: A facility cannot mature before it was written.

checks.name: custom::remaining_maturity_never_rises
checks.description: Months to maturity counts down, never up.

checks.name: custom::default_not_before_acquisition
checks.description: A default cannot precede the day the portfolio bought it.

checks.name: custom::recovery_not_before_default
checks.description: A workout cannot resolve before the default that caused it.

checks.name: custom::sale_not_before_acquisition
checks.description: A facility cannot be sold before it was bought.

checks.name: custom::default_flag_matches_credit_state
checks.description: The flag and the state must agree.

checks.name: custom::ccc_flag_matches_rating
checks.description: The CCC flag and the rating bucket must agree.

checks.name: custom::terminal_states_are_the_last_row
checks.description: A facility that prepaid, matured, was sold or recovered stops reporting.

checks.name: custom::prepaid_and_matured_balances_are_zero
checks.description: Nothing is still owed once the facility has left.

checks.name: custom::no_acquisition_after_reinvestment_end
checks.description: The manager stops buying when the reinvestment period closes.

checks.name: custom::recovery_never_exceeds_defaulted_par
checks.description: A workout cannot return more than was owed when the facility defaulted. Measured against `par_at_default`, not `current_par` — a resolved facility carries no par, so the live figure is zero by then.

checks.name: custom::a_facility_keeps_its_obligor
checks.description: A facility cannot change which company borrowed it.

checks.name: custom::obligor_holds_more_than_one_facility
checks.description: The pool is genuinely grouped. If every obligor held exactly one facility the grouping would be doing nothing, and every concentration figure would silently be a per-facility figure.

checks.name: custom::shares_are_between_zero_and_one
checks.description: Every `share_where` and `max_group_share` metric is a fraction of par, so none can leave [0, 1]. A share above 1 means the numerator was drawn from a different population than the denominator, which is the failure a reported percentage hides best.

checks.name: custom::bullet_balance_does_not_amortise
checks.description: A bullet facility repays at maturity, so while it is performing the balance holds flat.
